quest.title: The Recollector's Path
quest.description: Sorush's training continues. Even a Wenut crystallized across countless eras has a date of expiry. Could there possibly be an ode or poem that could outlast even such a being?\n
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x10, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Hm. Looks like you successfully completed your training.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we got it done, but ugh, Sorush...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After seeing that crystallized Wenut, she said, with real sincerity, that even though it had existed for centuries, one day it would still disappear without a trace...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then immediately afterward, when we mentioned that her odes might be distorted as well, her mood changed instantly.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmph. But of course! My deeds... I mean, the deeds of us Pari should be eternal. How can such a thing be compared to that which might part into dust and ash?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: If something cannot be recorded properly, then there must be something wrong with the method. You wished to remind me of this fact, which is why you sent me to view the crystallized Wenut. Am I right, Elder Zurvan?

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Ah. That's the way you see it. Interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Do you care nothing for the renown of the Pari?

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: If you're speaking of renown in the way humans understand it, not so much. Whatever you say, the present-day members of the Order of Skeptics are so very dull.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: #Of course, if there are more interesting individuals like {NICKNAME} or Paimon, then that would be a different case entirely.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hold... Y—You can't call her "Elder"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sorush, there's no need to be stingy. Zurvan is the eldest here, so us calling her elder is reasonable, right?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Alright. Enough idle chatter. If Sorush still thinks so highly of this "human notion of renown," then the training that comes next might be just right.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Alright. I await your good news.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: It is by my standards.

talks.objective: Head to the specified location and complete the trial
Head to the specified location and complete the trial

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, isn't this the place we passed by looking for Mihir? Though, Mihir shouldn't be here right now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All those thorns... They should be Mihir's companions. They look pretty good. Speaking of which, they helped us a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Pale Floater... Did you forget all that I have accomplished?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No way. You might complain a lot, but you do care about your people, right?

choices.text: I... What did you do, Sorush? I can't seem to recall.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: How can you be so forgetful, Yasnapati? I punish you with the task of several more odes!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha. Paimon knew it! You've got a big bark to go with your soft heart.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Malicious slander! I was only here because I wished to earn the Chaplet. If the elder hadn't made me come... Hmph.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, whatever you say, Mihir's part of the reason you even managed to claim the Twin-Horned Chaplet. Shouldn't you thank her for that, at least?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Her? Bah. For such a figure, one stained and still struggling thusly, I'd say she would only be worth any merit after another ten cleansing pilgrimages.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ten is way too many! Uh... Wait a minute, on second thought, Paimon thinks it wouldn't be too hard...

choices.text: The path really isn't that long.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, maybe we can use it as exercise every now and again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From the name, Paimon thought we would be walking for ten days and nights. As it turns out, we didn't even need to go that far. Hmm... the shortness of this trail is making Paimon suspicious.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: If it was as long as the Oceanids' pilgrimage, then perhaps I would respect her. As it stands now, I can only state that the distance of the cleansing pilgrimage suits Mihir.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Oceanids' pilgrimage?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: After the catastrophe, a great number of Oceanids came from Fontaine to Sumeru, with the path they walked becoming their so-called holy path.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Strange. Why would the Oceanids need to come to Sumeru? Pilgrimage... A pilgrimage for what?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hm... I only heard of such a thing from my elder. Though there have been Oceanids from Fontaine, I haven't truly looked into it...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Could it be for the Harvisptokhm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right. Sorush said that the Harvisptokhm was the god that let the Pari be born. If honor's a big deal here, then the thing most deserving of it is definitely the Harvisptokhm.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what's the potential relationship between the Oceanids and the Harvisptokhm...? Don't tell Paimon the Oceanids and Pari are like, distantly related?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Looking at you carefully, Paimon's really beginning to see the resemblance!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha. Paimon hasn't discovered any world-shaking secrets, has she?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The slander flows from your lips again, Pale Floater... I know nothing of any Oceanid.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hm. You're probably right. Sorush did say that the distance Oceanids need to travel for their pilgrimage is far longer than Mihir's cleansing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if that's true, does that mean the Oceanids are stronger than the Pari? Is Sorush admitting defeat? Hehe.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Wh—What? I didn't mean that...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...In all seriousness, the "cleansing pilgrimage" is not actually tied to distance. It is more of a symbolic affair, showcasing a rise and return to form.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... That sounds impressive... but...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Regardless, it is irrational to brush all Pari as lesser than the Oceanids! And not because of any bias I may or may not have regarding Mihir.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, why did Zurvan say that the next part of the training was just right for Sorush? It doesn't look like anything special here. Also, Mihir's missing too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Though if she was here, Sorush probably wouldn't talk to her properly either. They are pretty different in a lot of ways.

choices.text: One is round and the other is pricky?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, but... But that's not what Paimon wanted to say!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: That fool... If her existence and her efforts over these centuries are forgotten, then what was it all for?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe that's the question that Zurvan wants Sorush to think about?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It seems that Sorush still needs some time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. She also said that being forgotten is a good thing.

choices.text: Though the way isn't long, running it repeatedly does make me tired...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Huh? I expected an adventurer to be used to such a life by now.

choices.text: Sorush's the hero of this story.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Indeed, hehe.
